rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inclined the Anṣār to accept the Qur’an wholeheartedly and sacrifice everything to protect it, one historical means by which His preservation promise was fulfilled.
rows.anchor: inclined the hearts of the Anṣā r towards it; they whole-heartedly accepted it and sacrificed everything to protect it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording that God Himself sent the Book down carries double emphasis.
rows.anchor: has a double emphasis in it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s duty is to convey the Book, not to make people accept it; it was not sent at his request.
rows.anchor: he does not have the responsibility to make people accept it. His responsibility is to only convey it to others.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preserving the Book intact is God’s responsibility, and history shows the many ways He fulfilled this promise.
rows.anchor: As far as keeping it intact and its protection is concerned, God will take care of it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier messengers were mocked too; the Prophet’s nation repeats a familiar pattern and will share the predecessors’ fate.
rows.anchor: What he is experiencing today from his nation is nothing new; previous prophets too faced a similar response from their nations.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Insolent wrongdoers cannot bear the messengers’ preaching: it pierces their hearts, so they evade it and refuse faith.
rows.anchor: Such is the nature of the preaching of God’s messengers that insolent wrongdoers cannot digest it easily.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a demanded heavenly sign would not make them believe; desire and arrogance, rather than lack of miracles, keep them from listening.
rows.anchor: the real reason is that they are not ready to give up their desires and because of arrogance are not ready to listen to the Prophet (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next passage points to signs in the world and within people that attest to the Prophet’s message; nature’s miracles make new demanded miracles unnecessary, since every part of the universe can guide the perceptive to God.
rows.anchor: in the presence of the miracles of nature, no new miracles are needed. If people have keen eyes and brains, every object of this universe can take them closer to God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intellect is the means through which guidance enters the heart; those who blind it cannot receive guidance.
rows.anchor: passage that makes guidance enter the heart is the intellect.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ratq means ‘closed’ and fataq means ‘to open.’
rows.anchor: the heavens and the earth both are closed. Then We open them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens are closed when they send no rain and the earth when no vegetation sprouts; God opens both, sending rain and bringing barren land to life.
rows.anchor: the heavens are closed and do no not rain down water. Similarly, the earth is closed and no vegetation sprouts from it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those denying monotheism or the afterlife, including people demanding a sign, should observe the daily signs God has made clear to guide them.
rows.anchor: those who deny monotheism and the hereafter and demand a sign to make them convinced observe signs that they encounter everyday.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflection on these observations reveals the Qur’an’s arguments for the beliefs it calls its audience to accept.
rows.anchor: in this observation are found the arguments presented by the Qur’ān in favour of what it wants its addressees to believe in.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain from the heavens revives the earth in a coordinated pair; this harmony shows that both share one Creator and controller, supporting monotheism.
rows.anchor: This harmony found between the two – as if they are pairs – clearly evidences the fact that both have the same creator who controls them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since dry, dead land is restored to life, resurrection after death should not be considered improbable; Sūrah Qāf makes the same connection.
rows.anchor: If a dry and dead piece of land is once again brought back to life, why should being re-created after death be regarded as improbable?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s elaborate provision of the heavens, earth, sun, moon, clouds, and winds for human benefit implies that He will hold people accountable for these favours.
rows.anchor: So how is it possible that He will let them go like this without holding them accountable for these favours.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rawāsiya is an adjective for mountains so established in usage that it functions as the noun itself.
rows.anchor: This attribute has become so famous for them that it has assumed the place of the very noun it qualifies.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A word is understood as omitted before the phrase ‘that it may not tilt with them.’
rows.anchor: a word to the effect 8 is suppressed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fijāj is the plural of fijj, meaning a space or gap between two mountains.
rows.anchor: the latter refers to the space or gap between two mountains.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mountain passes let people travel and trade between places instead of remaining confined to their own territories.
rows.anchor: it would not have been possible for anyone travel and do trade.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Finding the way means both navigating the physical passes and being guided by God’s great signs to recognize His power, exaltedness, and wisdom.
rows.anchor: God has made evident His great signs so that their eyes are opened, the majesties of His power, exaltedness and wisdom become clear and they find their way to Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are so blind that they fail to take guidance from a mountain yet expect a demanded miracle to guide them.
rows.anchor: How can people see a mole if they are unable to see a mountain?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great signs of earth are meant to prompt insight and remembrance; only the attentive can benefit, while the inattentive remain blind.
rows.anchor: God’s real purpose of showing these great signs is that people have insight and they are reminded. However, they can only benefit those who are attentive to them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heaven is a flawless, secure roof whose creation is ancient and which has remained intact, with no fissure or decay.
rows.anchor: No one knows when this roof was made and even after the passage of time, it has not become decrepit or inflicted with any flaw.

rows.speaker: Some exegetes
rows.claim: Some exegetes understand the heaven’s being ‘secure’ to mean that it is protected from the interference of devils.
rows.anchor: Some exegetes have interpreted the

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are abundant, but they cannot benefit people who have shut their eyes to them.
rows.anchor: there is no dearth of them; yet what can they serve such people who have shut their eyes from them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night, day, sun, and moon complement one another in harmony, showing that one governing intelligence made them serve the world’s collective benefit.
rows.anchor: they are complementing one another and are in total harmony with one another. This is evidence enough to show that this universe is being government by a single mind

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kull here refers to the sun and moon; in this construction it identifies a noun already mentioned, whether there are two or more referents.
rows.anchor: When the word w (each) occurs in this way, it becomes an instrument for defining a noun and refers to it as mentioned regardless of being two or more.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon keep their prescribed paths with minute precision; deviation would disrupt the universe, proving their submission to its master.
rows.anchor: They follow their course with minute precision and continue to do so with this perfection. This bears evidence to the fact that they obey the master of this universe.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Demanding another sign despite obvious celestial signs is foolish, and worshipping the sun or moon is especially so because they visibly submit.
rows.anchor: Even worse are those who have regarded the sun and the moon as deities even though they by their very existence continuously show that they are submissive.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents mock the Prophet’s humanity and status and demand a proof of his messengership; the signs of 21:30–33 answer that demand.
rows.anchor: how can he be God’s messenger when he is a human being; he also has no distinction over them in wealth and status.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following passage assures the Prophet to ignore their mockery: time will reveal his claims’ truth and dissolve their arrogance.
rows.anchor: Time is approaching when they will see the veracity of every claim he is making and all their arrogance will vanish.

rows.speaker: Exegetes
rows.claim: Exegetes generally interpret the lām in ‘for the Day of Judgement’ as carrying a temporal sense (‘on/in’).
rows.anchor: Exegetes have generally interpreted the ل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi instead takes the lām as indicating consequence and objective: the Day of Judgement is necessary to manifest God’s justice, not an end in itself.
rows.anchor: In my opinion, it signifies the consequence and objective. In other words, for the manifestation of the consequence of the Day of Judgement, God will place the balance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun of kāna is understood as omitted because the context supplies it.
rows.anchor: is suppressed because of concomitant indication.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun in ‘we brought it forth’ refers to the mustard seed (ḥabba).
rows.anchor: The feminine pronoun in َﺗَﻴۡﻨَﺎ ﺑﻬَﺎ refers to ﺣَﺒ	َﺔٍ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God needs no helper to account for people; it is mistaken to think accounting exceeds His power or that He depends on deities for hidden information.
rows.anchor: If people think that this task is beyond Him, then this is their misunderstanding. And if some others think that He is dependent on their deities to find out information only they are privy too, then this again is a wrong notion.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After 21:24’s reference to the teaching of earlier prophets, the passage names prophets who founded nations: Moses first as the last prior law-bearing messenger, with Aaron as helper; then Abraham and his descendants’ two branches, followed by Noah.
rows.anchor: those prophets are mentioned in a sequence who were the founders of their respective nations. Just before Muḥammad (sws), Moses (sws) was the messenger who was bestowed sharī‘ah from God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham is presented as founder and leader of the Israelite and Ishmaelite branches, explaining the allusions to Isaac, Jacob, and Lot in this sequence.
rows.anchor: Abraham (sws) is mentioned who was the founder of nations and the leader of both branches of his progeny – the Israelites and the Ishmaelites.
